title: feat(021): Phase A: extraction, kernel-native adjudication, the live Decision ledger
body:
## What

Spec 021 (kernel-native consumption) authored and implemented whole: Phase A of the enforcement seam (spec 001 §4.6, §5 item 1). The substrate now produces its own governed model, boots the published governance kernel from it, adjudicates every Rust-routed operation, and records denials in a hash-linked Decision ledger.

## The three deliverables

**Extraction from day one.** `enrahitu-extract` (toolchain, spec 018) decodes the tsparser meta (protobufjs over proto copies carried by the package; the vendored tsparser is untouched), lowers it with the new capability manifest `app-manifest.json` into `app-model.json` per spec 020, and verifies before emitting: schema-valid, arrays sorted per `x-sortKey`, cross-refs resolve, observed usage subset-of declared (a transitive import walk mapping named facade imports to capability kinds), and the fork 3 ban-list (raw addon/driver/fetch/secret bindings only at their designated sites). Sealing pins `gate.configHash` via the kernel and closes the cross-language hash loop with the `genesisPayload` oracle: a model only emits if the Rust kernel already accepts it. The committed model is a governed derived artifact: `enrahitu-extract --check` exits 2 on staleness or hand-edits, and `verify.yml` runs it after the app build.

**The kernel at the napi boundary.** `@statecrafting/kernel-native` 0.1.0 from npm. Boot is synchronous at module evaluation, fail-closed on the nine refusals, write-once per process. One `demand()` call guards the seams: the CoreLedger driver proxy (`query`/`execute`/`batch`/`transaction` as `db.read`/`db.write`/`db.migrate`/`db.txn`, inner tx re-wrapped), the governed hiq facade (exact kv/counter kinds with the key attribute, so the rate limiter's `keyPrefix: "rl:"` constraint is enforced for real), the secret accessors (`secret.read` per secret), and governed egress (idp proxy on `rauthy-upstream`, OIDC round-trips on `rauthy-issuer`). A deny is `APIError.permissionDenied` with a `KERNEL_DENIED` detail naming the capability; raw handlers answer 403. Acting-service attribution: explicit arg, then `runAsService` scope, then `currentRequest()`; unattributable is denied.

**The Decision ledger live.** Append-only `kernel_decisions` table through a raw driver (the enforcement plane sits beneath its own gate by construction: no recursion). The deploy genesis anchors the chain to the booted model hash; denials append as `decision/v1` records; `verifyChain` re-verifies the persisted chain. Routine allows do not append: the ledger records governance events, not traffic.

## Spec amendments riding this change (the coupling gate's demand)

001 (§5 item 1 marked landed), 002 (hiq facade), 003 (driver seam), 004 (secrets/rate-limit/boot hooks), 005 (governed egress), 010 (CI staleness step), 018 (extract stage packaging). Derived shards regenerated and committed.

## Scope guards honored

`template.toml` and spec 009 untouched (the model is the sibling of the stamp contract, never its replacement). Frontend/dashboard/observability are §5 item 2, not here (`observability.otel` records `false` honestly until that spec lands). `vendor/encore` stays MPL-2.0 at file level; no vendor patch.

## Verification

- `spec-spine compile` / `index` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `couple` all green (43 paths, no drift).
- `npm run typecheck` green; `npm test` 88 passed, 11 skipped (the Postgres arm runs here in CI).
- `enrahitu-extract --check` exit 0 on the committed model; probed exit 2 on a hand-edit and exit 1 on a seeded ceiling violation.
- Kernel smoke: allow on declared ceiling, `kernel:deny:capability:undeclared` on excess, `kernel:deny:constraint:keyPrefix` on a non-`rl:` counter key.

Closes statecrafting spec 004 acceptance item 3's consumer condition: the suite builds green against the published package (recorded in the statecrafting corpus separately, per that spec's own instruction).

- A `manifest` job stitches the two per-arch images into the pullable multi-arch tags (`:<sha>`, `:latest`, and the release tag) via `docker buildx imagetools`, so `docker pull` resolves per host arch.
- Triggers gain `release: published` alongside the existing `workflow_dispatch` + weekly schedule. `packages: write` is scoped to the workflow, which never runs on a PR, so a fork can never push.

## Governance

Spec 016 §3/§4 gain the publish behavior + acceptance; §5 drops the now-realized "registry publishing out of scope (stagecraft side)" line; the spec **reopens to `in-progress`** until a published image has actually been pulled and verified (2026-07-16 Status note). Coupling: 2 paths, no drift.

## Verification

YAML validated; `spec-spine compile/index/lint --fail-on-warn/index check` green; `tsc --noEmit` clean. The publish itself is verified by running the workflow (dispatch/release) and pulling the resulting `ghcr.io/stagecraft-ing/enrahitu` image, which flips 016 back to complete.

title: fix(018): make the toolchain publish workflow idempotent
body:
## What

Makes the `publish` workflow (spec 018) idempotent so a template-release tag that does not change the toolchain does not fail.

## Why

The `v0.2.0` tag triggered `publish`, which tried to `npm publish` the `@enrahitu/*` toolchain + addon packages. They are independently versioned (spec 018 versioning rule) and unchanged since v0.1.0, so npm rejected re-publishing `0.1.0`:

> npm error You cannot publish over the previously published versions: 0.1.0.

All three matrix jobs failed; nothing new was published. Per the spec, `0.1.0` is correct for those packages (the v0.2.0 work touched no `vendor/encore` or `addon/src`), so the bug is the workflow, not the versions.

## Fix

Each of the four publish steps now checks the registry (`npm view <pkg>@<version>`) and publishes only when that exact version is not already there. A template-only release is a clean no-op; a genuine toolchain version bump still publishes normally.

## After merge

Re-run `publish` (workflow_dispatch) to confirm it goes green against the current package versions.

typecheck + vitest (69 passed) + spine gates + actionlint all green.

title: feat(013): project-site base path + flavor-agnostic Pages build
body:
## What

Makes the born-with GitHub Pages workflow (spec 013) work for a **project** Pages site (`https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/`), not just a user/org site or a custom domain, and makes it flavor-agnostic.

- **Project base path.** `pages.yml` sets `PAGES_BASE=/<repo>/` (overridable via a `PAGES_BASE` repo variable; set it to `/` for a user/org site or a custom domain) as each frontend flavor's Vite `base`. The React flavor also feeds it to the `createBrowserRouter` `basename` via `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`. A `404.html` copy of `index.html` gives client-side deep links an SPA fallback.
- **Flavor-agnostic.** The install and build steps resolve whichever frontend flavor directory the stamped app kept (`frontend/` or `frontend-react/`) instead of hardcoding `frontend/`, so a react-stamped app's Pages build works (spec 015 prunes `frontend/` for react stamps).
- **No image impact.** The container and dev builds leave `PAGES_BASE` unset, so `base` stays `/` and the built artifact is unchanged.

## Why

Both flavors' `vite.config.ts` defaulted Vite `base` to `/`, and `pages.yml` hardcoded the Vue `frontend/` directory. A project Pages site would 404 every hashed asset, and a react-stamped app's Pages build would fail on the pruned `frontend/`.

## Verification

- `PAGES_BASE=/demo-app/` builds (both flavors) emit asset URLs under `/demo-app/` and write a `404.html`; the React bundle bakes in the `/demo-app/` basename. An unset `PAGES_BASE` builds at base `/`, matching the container build.
- `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 69 passed / 11 skipped; `actionlint` clean on `pages.yml`.
- `spec-spine compile && index && lint --fail-on-warn && index check && couple` all green.

## Governance

Still out of the factory contract (no `template.toml` change): Pages stays a born-with, off-by-default CI capability. Amends spec 013 and couples the owning specs for the touched files: 006 (`frontend/vite.config.ts`) and 015 (`frontend-react/`).

title: feat(018): export-ignore the vendored toolchain so it leaves the stamped tree
body:
## What

Realize spec 018's stated design that *"the vendored Encore source ... leaves the stamped tree"* (§1/§2), which nothing had implemented.

`git archive` (the mechanism the Stagecraft factory uses to export a stamp, spec 005) was carrying **all 625 `vendor/encore` files** into every stamp, because no `export-ignore` existed. Found via a local dry-run of the factory's stamp export against a real target.

## Change

Add `export-ignore` to `.gitattributes` for the heavy `vendor/encore` build-source subtrees (`tsparser`, `miniredis`, `proto`, `runtimes/core`, `runtimes/js/{src,build.rs}`, and the workspace Cargo manifests), **mirroring the existing `.dockerignore` exclusions**. `vendor/encore/runtimes/js/encore.dev` (the JS runtime a stamped app resolves through the `node_modules` symlink) is deliberately kept, exactly as `.dockerignore` keeps it.

## Effect

A `git archive` stamp drops **861 → 441 tracked files** (`vendor/` 625 → 197), removing ~190K lines of toolchain build-source that no stamped app reads or builds (it consumes the published `@enrahitu/toolchain` packages). This closes the `vendor/` half of 018's slimmed-tree target; the `addon/` Rust-source half remains, on the same mechanism.

## Verification

- `git archive --worktree-attributes HEAD | tar -t`: `vendor/` count **625 → 197**; `tsparser` / `runtimes/core` excluded (0), `encore.dev` kept (195).
- `spec-spine compile && index && lint`: 0 errors/warnings; `.derived` regenerated.
- `spec-spine couple --base origin/main --head HEAD`: **OK, no drift**.
- No code change (`.gitattributes` + spec + derived only), so `verify` (typecheck + test) is unaffected.

The spec 018 body + acceptance + status are amended to record the mechanism.

title: fix(016): keep host build:addon for the addon JS loader in image.yml
body:
## Summary

Third `image.yml` iteration. The glibc fix (#13) got the amd64 job past
the addon and runtime builds, but `docker-build.sh` then failed with
`missing addon/index.js`.

`docker-build.sh` injects three addon files: the `.node`, `index.js`, and
`index.d.ts`. The latter two are the napi-generated JS loader/types, which
are **gitignored** (regenerated by `npm run build:addon`). My #13 change
replaced the host `npm run build:addon` with the cargo-only
`build-addon-linux.sh`, which emits only the `.node` -> the loader files
went missing on a clean checkout.

Fix: restore the host `npm run build:addon` before the bookworm
cross-build. `build:addon` emits the arch-independent loader plus a native
`.node`; `build-addon-linux.sh` then overwrites the `.node` with the
glibc-matched one. This is the documented "build:addon (host) + the linux
cross-build" flow.

(The arm64 job in the #13 run hit an unrelated transient apt failure at
"Install protoc + cmake"; it clears on re-run.)

## Testing

- `actionlint` (all workflows) PASS; spine `compile` / `lint` /
  `index check` / `couple` all green (`couple`: 2 paths, no drift).
- The cargo cross-build itself is already verified locally (#13 produced a
  valid bookworm-glibc arm64 `.node`); the full amd64/arm64 build+smoke is
  the re-dispatched `image.yml`, which I will shepherd to green.

title: fix(016): build the addon in bookworm so its glibc matches the image
body:
## Summary

With the ownership fix (#11), `image.yml` built the image on both arches,
but the smoke failed: the container booted rauthy fine, then the app
crashed on startup loading the hiqlite addon:

```
Error: /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
       (required by /workspace/addon/hiqlite-native.linux-arm64-gnu.node)
```

`image.yml` built the addon **natively** on `ubuntu-24.04` (glibc 2.39),
but the runtime image is `node:24-slim` (Debian bookworm, glibc 2.36). The
runtime `.so` was already fine (it builds in `rust:1-bookworm`); the addon
was the odd one out.

Fix: a new `build-addon-linux.sh` cross-builds the addon in
`rust:1-bookworm`, exactly like the runtime. Since the addon's `build.rs`
runs `napi_build::setup()`, a plain `cargo build --release` emits a
working N-API module; the script renames the cdylib to the platform
`.node` (as root inside the container, so a non-root runner isn't blocked).
`image.yml` now uses it instead of the native `npm run build:addon`.

## Testing

- `bash -n` + `actionlint` (all workflows) PASS. Spine gate: `compile` /
  `lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check` / `couple` all green (`couple`:
  4 paths, no drift).
- Verifying the script locally (arm64 bookworm build produces a valid
  linux-arm64 ELF `.node`), and the full amd64/arm64 build+smoke by
  re-dispatching `image.yml` after merge, which I will shepherd to green.

title: fix(017): generate JWT dev keys in the e2e globalSetup
body:
## Summary

With the hydration fix (#10) in place, the e2e got past rauthy's login
form on CI but the OIDC callback then returned 500. Root cause: the token
exchange succeeded, but `finalizeLogin` signs the session token with the
RS256 keypairs in `keys/*.pem` (`backend/lib/jwt.ts` ->
`accessPrivateKey()`/`refreshPrivateKey()`), and a clean CI checkout has
no JWT keys. `globalSetup` synced only the rauthy client secret, never the
JWT keypairs; locally the pems pre-existed, which hid the gap.

Fix: `globalSetup` now runs `npm run generate-keys` before booting the
stack. The ledger needs no such step (it self-creates its dir + schema).

## Testing

- **Reproduced the CI condition locally**: deleted the four `keys/*.pem`
  (leaving only `rauthy-client-secret`, exactly the CI state). Without the
  fix the callback 500s; with it `globalSetup` regenerates the keys and
  `npm run test:e2e` passes the full round-trip (login -> callback ->
  `/me` -> CSRF logout -> 401, no off-origin requests), 1.7s.
- Spine gate: `compile` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check` /
  `couple` all green (`couple`: 2 paths, no drift).
- Confirms on the nightly path itself by re-dispatching `e2e.yml` after
  merge, which I will shepherd to green.

title: fix(018): clean cross-build .ts files inside the container
body:
## Summary

The first `image.yml` run (spec 016) failed on both arches at the linux
runtime cross-build. The cargo build itself **succeeded** (11m36s); the
failure was the cleanup step:

```
find: cannot delete '.../target-linux/.../CMakeFiles/zlib.dir/compiler_depend.ts': Permission denied
```

`build-runtime-linux.sh` deletes CMake's stray `*.ts` dependency-tracking
files (they choke the Encore tsparser app walk) on the **host** after the
container build. But those files are created by **root** inside the
`rust:1-bookworm` container, so on a non-root Linux CI runner the
host-side `find -delete` hits Permission denied and takes the whole build
down. macOS Docker Desktop remaps bind-mount ownership to the host user,
which is why this passed on dev machines.

Fix: do the `.ts` cleanup **inside** the container, where it runs as root.

## Testing

- `bash -n` OK. Spine gate: `compile` / `lint --fail-on-warn` /
  `index check` / `couple` all green (`couple`: 2 paths, no drift).
- This path only manifests on a non-root Linux host, so the real check is
  re-dispatching `image.yml` after merge, which I will shepherd to green.
- `verify`/`govern` here are unaffected: `verify` builds the runtime via
  `npm run build:runtime` (host cargo), not this cross-build script.

title: fix(017): wait for rauthy login page to hydrate before submitting
body:
## Summary

The spec 017 login e2e passed locally but failed on the first nightly
`e2e.yml` run in CI. Root cause, confirmed from the Playwright trace: the
failing POST to `/auth/v1/oidc/authorize` carried
`content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (a **native** form
submit), not rauthy's intended client-side JSON fetch. On slower CI
runners the test clicked "Login" before rauthy's SPA hydrated and attached
its `onsubmit` handler, so the browser did a plain form POST that rauthy
rejects with "Content type error"; the password step then never appeared.

Fix:
- Wait for the rauthy page to load **and hydrate** (`networkidle`, which
  also covers its proof-of-work challenge fetch) before filling the form.
- Give web-first assertions a CI-tolerant timeout (`expect.timeout: 15s`,
  and 20s for the two-step password field).
- Document the hydration requirement in spec 017 section 3.

## Testing

- Local `npm run test:e2e`: **1 passed** (1.5s); `networkidle` settles
  cleanly, no regression to the full round-trip.
- Spine gate: `compile` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check` /
  `couple` all green (`couple`: 3 paths, no drift).
- The definitive check is the nightly path itself: I will re-dispatch
  `e2e.yml` after merge and shepherd it to green (it cannot run on a PR).

title: feat(016): linux/amd64 image support + native multi-arch CI
body:
## Summary

Implements spec 016: linux/amd64 support for the single-container image, so
the template can land on the fleet's x86-64 nodes (milestone M3), not just
the arm64 dev Macs.

- **`scripts/docker-build.sh`** (spec 007): the `[arch]` argument now drives
  `docker build --platform linux/<arch>` on **both** the base and final
  images. Previously it only selected the injected native artifacts, so
  `docker-build.sh amd64` on an arm64 host silently built an arm64 image
  with amd64 `.node`/`.so` inside. The injected addon `.node` and runtime
  `.so` are now ELF-arch-checked (`file`), so a mismatch fails the build,
  not the first request (spec 016 section 3).
- **`.github/workflows/image.yml`** (spec 016): builds and smokes both
  arches **natively** on their own runners (amd64 on `ubuntu-24.04`, arm64
  on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`), so no QEMU: build the addon + linux runtime,
  assemble via `docker-build.sh`, then `docker run` and assert `/health` +
  `/hiq/health` after first-boot secret provisioning. `workflow_dispatch` +
  weekly, so the long build never gates a push but cannot silently rot.

Spec 016 section 2 is reconciled with the post-018 toolchain relocation
(`build-runtime-linux.sh` already takes the arch arg and lives under
`packages/toolchain/`, so it needed no change).

## Testing

- Static: `actionlint` (all workflows) PASS; `bash -n scripts/docker-build.sh`
  OK. Spine gate: `compile` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check` /
  `couple` all green (`couple`: 4 paths, no drift; 016 no longer an index
  orphan).
- Verified the smoke targets the right surface: the container app listens on
  `:8080` (`docker/entrypoint.sh`, `infra.config.json` `base_url`), and
  first-boot completing is what makes `/health` return 200.

**amd64 build + smoke verification** runs on native x86-64/arm64 hardware via
`image.yml`, which is `workflow_dispatch`/schedule only and therefore cannot
execute on this PR. I will dispatch it on `main` after merge and shepherd it
to green. The local-Mac emulated cross-build (spec 016 section 4, bullet 1)
stays delegated: it is the same `docker-build.sh` code path under QEMU, and
building the addon for linux on a Mac has no cross-build script today.

Note: `verify`/`govern` here validate the coupling and that the change does
not break the build/tests; they do not run `image.yml`.

title: feat(017): browser-real rauthy login e2e (Playwright)
body:
## Summary

Implements spec 017: an end-to-end Playwright test that drives the full
rauthy login topology in a real browser engine, closing the highest-value
gap in the template's confidence story.

`e2e/login.rauthy.spec.ts` walks: SPA `/` -> "Sign in with rauthy" ->
same-origin `/auth/*` proxy (spec 005) -> rauthy's two-step login form ->
OIDC callback -> `access_token`/`refresh_token` cookies -> `GET
/api/v1/auth/me` shows the user -> CSRF-guarded `POST /logout` -> `/me` is
401. It also asserts **no request ever left the app origin** (`:4000`),
which is what proves the same-origin proxy topology.

- **Out of the verify verb** (spec 017 section 3). Runs via `npm run
  test:e2e` and `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` (workflow_dispatch + nightly),
  `retries: 0` so a flake fails loudly. `globalSetup` boots dev rauthy
  (compose + client-secret sync); the app runs under Playwright's
  `webServer` with the rauthy driver enabled.
- **Image build** (spec 007): `e2e/` joins the frontend flavors dropped
  from the image worktree, since `@playwright/test` is a devDep absent
  under `npm ci --omit=dev`.
- **Root shell config** (spec 001): `test:e2e` script, `@playwright/test`
  devDep, and `tsconfig.json`/`vitest.config.ts` exclude `e2e/`.

## Testing

Ran the browser-real suite locally end to end against the pinned
`ghcr.io/sebadob/rauthy:0.36.0` container: **1 passed** (login -> callback
-> `/me` as `admin@localhost` -> CSRF logout -> 401, zero off-origin
requests). Bringing it up surfaced two real issues, now fixed in the
second commit:

- `RAUTHY_ISSUER` must end in a trailing slash (`.../auth/v1/`): rauthy
  0.36.0 advertises its issuer that way and openid-client v6 validates the
  discovery document's issuer exactly, so `getConfig()` threw and
  `rauthyLogin` returned 500. This aligns the e2e (and the `.env.example`
  dev hint) with `docker/entrypoint.sh` and spec 005, which already
  require it.
- Spread `process.env` into the Playwright `webServer.env` so the app
  child reliably sees the rauthy config.

Static gate: `actionlint` (all workflows) PASS; spine `compile` /
`lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check` / `couple` all green (`couple`: 13
paths, no drift; 017 no longer an index orphan). `npm ci --dry-run` exit
0; `encore.dev` stays `^1.57.9` (lock churn is purely additive: the
Playwright tree).

Note: `verify` and `govern` here do not execute the browser test by
design; it runs on the nightly `e2e` workflow (re-runnable now via
`gh workflow run e2e.yml` once merged).

title: feat(013): off-by-default GitHub Pages preview workflow
body:
## Summary

Implements spec 013 (LI-3 of the spec 010 absorption): a GitHub Pages
deployment slot stamped apps are born with. `pages.yml` publishes the
built SPA (`backend/web/dist`) as a zero-cost static preview.

- **Off by default.** Ships inert. A push to `main` with Pages disabled
  and `ENABLE_PAGES` unset evaluates the build job's `if` to false, so
  the run is skipped, never failed. Opt in by setting the Pages source to
  "GitHub Actions" (and optionally `ENABLE_PAGES=true` to publish on push).
- **needs-guard rule (spec 013 section 3, hard requirement).** `deploy`
  depends on `build` and carries no custom `if`, so the implicit
  `success()` guard holds: a skipped or failed build skips deploy. The
  header documents that any future `if` added to deploy must re-assert
  `needs.build.result == 'success'`.
- All four actions SHA-pinned with a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` (house style).
- Not part of the factory template contract (spec 009 holds Pages out of
  scope); this is CI-side only, no `template.toml` change.

## Testing

- `actionlint .github/workflows/pages.yml` and `actionlint` (all
  workflows): PASS.
- Spine gate: `compile` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check` /
  `couple --base origin/main` all green; `couple` checks 2 paths, no
  drift. Spec 013 is no longer an index orphan.
- Upload path confirmed: `frontend/vite.config.ts` `outDir` is
  `../backend/web/dist`, matching the `upload-pages-artifact` path.

## Known operator note

The SPA builds with vite `base` = `/`. On a *project* Pages URL
(`<org>.github.io/enrahitu/`) the absolute `/assets/...` references 404;
the preview renders correctly on a user/org Pages site or a custom
domain. Spec section 3 prescribes exactly these steps (no base-path
handling) and section 5 puts custom domains out of scope, so this is
faithful to the spec; a base-path follow-up could be a later spec.

title: feat(015): react-rr7 frontend flavor, selected by the scaffold verb
body:
## Spec 015: React + React Router v7 frontend flavor

Makes the `frontend` slot real by adding a second allowed value, `react-rr7`, as a
parallel SPA flavor directory. The chassis carries every flavor; the scaffold verb
keeps one and prunes the rest at stamp time.

### What shipped

- **`frontend-react/`**: React 19 + React Router v7 (SPA / data-router mode,

  with login state), `/login` (driver choice: mock + rauthy), `/profile`
  (`GET /api/v1/auth/me`, logout `Form` action, hiqlite cache demo widget).
  `src/lib/api.ts` is a byte-for-byte copy of the Vue client, so auth, CSRF, and
  API paths are identical across flavors (no flavor-specific auth path).
- **`template.toml`** (spec 009): `[slots].frontend.allowed` gains `react-rr7`;
  contract `0.4.0` to `0.5.0`.
- **`scripts/stamp.mjs`** (spec 014): the scaffold verb gained step 3, frontend
  flavor selection: prune the unselected flavor directory (`vue` to `frontend/`,
  `react-rr7` to `frontend-react/`) and repoint the root `build:web` / `dev:web`
  scripts at the survivor. Three new `stamp.test.ts` cases.
- **`spec-spine.toml`** (spec 000): `standalone_npm_packages` gains `frontend-react`.
- **root `tsconfig.json` / `vitest.config.ts`** (spec 001): exclude `frontend-react/`
  alongside `frontend/`; the SPA flavors typecheck and test under their own manifests.

### Verification

- React app builds into `backend/web/dist`; served by `npm run dev` on :4000 with
  SPA history fallback (deep routes `/login`, `/profile` fall back to `index.html`).
- Full auth round-trip against the running app: mock login (Casey / Avery) to
  `/me` to logout, access cookie cleared, post-logout `/me` returns 401; CSRF
  enforced (headerless logout returns 400); hiqlite cache demo round-trips.
- Vue default flavor still builds; the scaffold verb prunes `frontend-react/` from
  a vue stamp (unit-tested).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, vitest 69 passed / 11 skipped, spine gates
  (`compile` / `index check` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `couple`) green with zero
  waivers.

### Delegated (consumer-side, per spec 019 / 014 precedent)

- Full image build + boot smoke (owned by the packaging pipeline, spec 007/008,
  and spec 016's amd64 work). The flavor's only runtime footprint is the built
  `backend/web/dist`, which `docker-build.sh` already copies from `build:web` output.

Specs amended in the same change: 015 (complete), 009, 014, 000, 001. Contract 0.5.0.

title: feat(014): scaffold verb stamps a fresh clone into a named app
body:
## Summary

Implements spec 014: the in-template **scaffold verb**, moving the stamping recipe out of factory-side folklore and into the template itself.

- **`scripts/stamp.mjs`** (new): run from the repo root of a fresh clone to turn it into a named app. Steps, per spec 014 §3:
  1. Validate slots against `template.toml [slots]` (name pattern, org required, frontend in the allowed list).
  2. Substitute `app_name` in `package.json` (root `name`) and `package-lock.json` (root `name` + `packages[""]`). Substrate names (`@enrahitu/*`, the addon crate) are left intact.
  3. Lockfile discipline: v0 stamping edits no dependencies, so no `npm install` runs (a future refresh must be `--package-lock-only`).
  4. Provenance: `--cert` is copied to `.stagecraft/born-with.json` and validated via `scripts/verify-born-with.mjs` (spec 012); a failing cert fails the stamp and is rolled back.
  5. Regenerate derived truth (`spec-spine compile && spec-spine index`) since the app name is a hashed input; a governed repo always regenerates, an absent binary hard-fails.
  6. Append a `## Stamped` lineage marker to `README.md` (idempotent: replaced, never duplicated).
  Dependency-free (node builtins only), so a stamped app runs it with nothing but node.
- **`template.toml`**: adds `scaffold = "node scripts/stamp.mjs"` under `[verbs]` and bumps `[contract].version` to **0.4.0**.
- **spec 009** (owner of `template.toml`): amended so the reserved scaffold verb is now live (contract v0.4).
- **spec 014**: marked `implementation: complete`; establishes `scripts/stamp.mjs` + `scripts/stamp.test.ts`.

Also fixes a latent bug in the direct-invocation guard: it compared `import.meta.url` against the raw `process.argv[1]`, which silently no-op'd under a symlinked checkout (macOS `/var`→`/private/var`); it now compares realpaths.

## Testing

title: fix(018): npm ci no longer fails on toolchain carrier lock entries
body:
## Summary

`verify` has been red on `main` since the v0.1.0 release. It dies at
`npm ci` (before any build) with `Invalid Version:`.

Root cause: `package-lock.json` recorded the three
`@enrahitu/toolchain-{darwin-arm64,linux-x64,linux-arm64}` carriers
**without a version** (placeholder entries from when they were
unpublished, `67aa8a8`). Once the v0.1.0 carriers went live on npm,
`npm ci` began resolving them and comparing the real `0.1.0` against the
empty lock version, throwing inside Arborist's dedup (`semver.eq("",
"0.1.0")`).

Fix: re-resolve the three carriers to proper lock entries (`version`,
`resolved`, `integrity`, `os`, `cpu`), so `npm ci` installs the
platform-matching one and skips the rest. Lock-only change; no manifest
or source touched.

## Testing

- `npm ci --dry-run` succeeds (previously threw `Invalid Version:`).
- `spec-spine compile` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check` /
  `couple --base origin/main`: all green (couple: 0 paths, no drift).
- This PR's own `verify` run exercises the real `npm ci` on linux.

title: feat(012): born-with provenance cert + validator (contract 0.3.0)
body:
## Summary

Implements spec 012 (born-with certificate + agentic posture binding,
LI-2 of spec 010): every stamped app is born with a provenance
certificate stating what it was stamped from and the agentic posture it
was born under. The template owns the cert schema and its validator; the
factory (stagecraft) emits the instance at stamp time.

- `.stagecraft/born-with.schema.json`: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). All
  fields required; `posture` is a closed enum; `defaulted` must be
  literally `false` (a cert admitting a defaulted posture is invalid by
  schema); `commit` is 40-hex; `stampedAt` is UTC.
- `scripts/verify-born-with.mjs`: dependency-free validator run with
  plain node (`node scripts/verify-born-with.mjs [path]`, default
  `.stagecraft/born-with.json`). Exit 0 valid and prints the cert's
  sha256 identity; exit 1 with reasons. The hash is sha256 over the
  recursively key-sorted, compact JSON, matching `canonical-keysort-json`
  so JS-side template code and Rust-side platform code hash identically.
- `template.toml`: adds the `[provenance]` table and bumps
  `[contract].version` 0.2.0 -> 0.3.0 (0.2.0 was already taken by spec
  018's `[requires].toolchain` key). Kept out of the `verify` verb: the
  template repo carries no cert of its own, so verify must pass without one.

Contract bookkeeping is co-edited with the owning spec 009 (§3.1/§3.3
record the table as landed at 0.3.0); spec 014's future scaffold-verb
bump is forward-corrected 0.3.0 -> 0.4.0 since 012 now occupies 0.3.0.

## Testing

- `scripts/verify-born-with.test.ts` drives the validator through its
  documented CLI: accepts a well-formed fixture and prints a stable
  sha256 matching an independently computed keysorted-JSON hash; rejects
  missing posture, `defaulted: true`, unknown posture, short commit,
  unexpected properties, and wrong `certVersion`.
- Local gate green: `spec-spine compile` (0 warnings),
  `lint --fail-on-warn` (0/0/0), `index check` (fresh),
  `couple --base origin/main` (8 paths, no drift).
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` green (9 files, 59 passed,
  11 skipped live-Postgres).
